question:
A manufacturing firm monitors its machinery temperature according to Newton’s Law of Cooling. Let $T(t)$ be the temperature of a machine at time $t$ minutes after being switched off. The machine is switched off when its temperature is $100^{\circ}C$, and the surrounding room temperature is $25^{\circ}C$. After 5 minutes, its temperature drops to $80^{\circ}C$.

(a) Formulate the differential equation describing this process.

(b) Find the temperature $T(t)$ as a function of time $t$.

(c) In how many minutes will the machine reach $40^{\circ}C$? Comment on when $T(t)$ will reach $25^{\circ}C$ according to this model.
explanation:
(a)

By Newton’s Law:

$\frac{dT}{dt} = -k(T-25)$

(b)

Rearranging and integrating:

$\frac{dT}{T-25} = -k dt$

$\int \frac{1}{T-25} dT = -k \int dt$

$\ln|T-25| = -kt + C$

$T-25 = Ce^{-kt}$

At $t=0,\ T=100$:

$100 - 25 = C \implies C = 75$

So, $T(t) = 25 + 75e^{-kt}$

At $t=5,\ T=80$:

$80 = 25 + 75e^{-5k}$

$55 = 75e^{-5k}$

$e^{-5k} = \frac{11}{15}$

$-5k = \ln \left( \frac{11}{15} \right)$

$k = -\frac{1}{5} \ln \left( \frac{11}{15} \right)$

(c)

Set $T(t)=40$:

$40 = 25 + 75e^{-kt}$

$15 = 75e^{-kt}$

$e^{-kt} = \frac{1}{5}$

$-kt = \ln \frac{1}{5}$

$t = \frac{-\ln \frac{1}{5}}{k}$

Plug in $k$:

$\ln \frac{1}{5} = -\ln 5\,\Rightarrow\, t = \frac{\ln 5}{-\frac{1}{5} \ln \frac{11}{15}}$

$\ln \frac{11}{15} \approx \ln 0.733 \approx -0.311$

So, $k \approx -\frac{1}{5} \times (-0.311) = 0.0622$

$t \approx \frac{1.609}{0.0622} \approx 25.86$ minutes

The machine will reach $40^{\circ}C$ after about $25.86$ minutes.

As $t \to \infty$, $e^{-kt} \to 0$, so $T(t) \to 25^{\circ}$ but never reaches it exactly. The machine will never attain room temperature exactly; it approaches $25^{\circ}C$ asymptotically.

options.A:
(a) $\frac{dT}{dt}=k(T-25)$
(b) $T(t)=25+75e^{kt}$
(c) $T=40^\circ C$ after about $5$ minutes; it reaches $25^\circ C$ exactly
options.B:
(a) $\frac{dT}{dt}=-k(T-25)$
(b) $T(t)=25+75e^{-kt}$, where $k=-\frac{1}{5}\ln\left(\frac{11}{15}\right)$
(c) $T=40^\circ C$ after about $25.86$ minutes; it approaches $25^\circ C$ asymptotically and never reaches it exactly
options.C:
(a) $\frac{dT}{dt}=-kT$
(b) $T(t)=100e^{-kt}$
(c) $T=40^\circ C$ after about $15.25$ minutes; it reaches $25^\circ C$ exactly
options.D:
(a) $\frac{dT}{dt}=-(T+25)$
(b) $T(t)=100-25t$
(c) $T=40^\circ C$ after about $2.4$ minutes; it becomes negative later
